Summarize sequential cohort attrition

Source: R/attrition.R
nis_attrition.Rd

Count the discharges that remain after each eligibility criterion.

Usage

nis_attrition(
  .data,
  ...,
  by_year = FALSE,
  weight_var = "DISCWT",
  .design = FALSE,
  .codes = NULL
)

nis_attrition_cohort(flow)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or lazy DuckDB query.

...

Named logical expressions applied cumulatively. Unnamed expressions use their deparsed text as the criterion label.

by_year

If TRUE, calculate each step within YEAR.

weight_var

Name of the discharge weight column. Defaults to "DISCWT".

.design

If TRUE, count only discharges with valid survey design fields, using the policy in nis_design(). Criteria still evaluate over the full ungrouped input. Use cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow) with the same input to build the survey design from the rules in flow. Use deterministic criteria, since they are evaluated by both functions.

.codes

Optional named list of code criteria applied after ..., in list order. Each criterion is a list with type ("dx" or "pr"), position, system, and codes (one flag definition). See nis_flag_dx() and nis_flag_pr() for the matching rules and definitions. Criterion names must be unique across ... and .codes.

flow

Result from nis_attrition(..., .design = TRUE).

Value

nis_attrition() returns a tibble with one initial row (step = 0) and one row per criterion. When by_year = TRUE, YEAR is the first column. With .design = TRUE, the initial row counts valid design discharges and the tibble stores the combined cohort expression. nis_attrition_cohort() extracts that expression for injection with !! into cohort in nis_design(). With .codes, attr(flow, "nis_criteria") is a tibble of criterion names and their code type, position, system, and definitions. These fields are missing for ordinary logical criteria. Pass the flow to nis_audit_code_transition() to summarize its code criteria by period.

Details

Evaluate criteria in order over the ungrouped input. Missing criteria exclude a discharge. Missing weights contribute zero to weighted counts. Use .design = TRUE when the same criteria will define a survey cohort. Use nis_attrition_cohort() to reuse the combined expression.

See also

Define and save a cohort, Define and save a cohort.

Other cohort-definition: nis_audit_code_transition(), nis_audit_dx_position(), nis_audit_prday(), nis_ccsr_codes(), nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_flag_pr_timing()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpwxUhgt/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpwxUhgt/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
flow <- nis_attrition(nis, adult = AGE >= 18, older = AGE >= 65, .design = TRUE)
flow
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>    step criterion               n_unweighted n_dropped_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <chr>                          <int>                <int>      <dbl>
#> 1     0 Valid design discharges           96                   NA      114. 
#> 2     1 adult                             96                    0      114. 
#> 3     2 older                             44                   52       52.5
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_dropped_weighted <dbl>, pct_retained <dbl>
nis_design(nis, cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow), keep = LOS)
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
#> Stratified 1 - level Cluster Sampling design (with replacement)
#> With (12) clusters.
#> Called via srvyr
#> Data variables: 
#>   - YEAR (int), HOSP_NIS (int), NIS_STRATUM (int), DISCWT (dbl), LOS (dbl)
